question: are SGO's temporal-information effects peculiar to SGO or general to population-based optimizers on GMPB

sgo_identity.name: Squid Game Optimizer
sgo_identity.reference: Azizi, Baghalzadeh Shishehgarkhaneh, Basiri, Moehler, Scientific Reports 13:5373 (2023)

benchmark.benchmark_seed: run index; identical environment trajectory for every optimizer and mode

modes.cold_restart: rebuild population and all algorithm state as a brand-new run; evaluate in the new environment
modes.previous_best_seeded: same fresh rebuild with exactly one slot replaced by that optimizer's own previous-environment best, re-evaluated in the new environment; no old objective value reused
modes.population_persistence: the native persistence path of the committed primary study, unchanged

PSO.note: standard PSO change reaction, matches official EDOLAB ChangeReaction_RPSO

WOA.note: leader X* reselected from refreshed costs

data_reuse.reproduction_runs: every reusable cell is re-executed to obtain the secondary diagnostics; each must reproduce its committed offline error exactly and is not new evidence

validation.note: committed CSVs must be read with float_precision='round_trip'; the pandas default parser is off by one ulp on 296 of 1488 rows

effects.sign_convention: lower offline error is better; negative E1 means seeding helps

secondary_diagnostics: normalised evaluation fraction to 50% and 90% recovery

statistics.pseudoreplication_control: environments aggregated within run before testing
statistics.cross_optimizer_family: SGO vs GWO, PSO, WOA, Holm corrected within each effect and case

prohibited: calling anything SGO-specific without cross-optimizer support
turning the study into a ranking of optimizers under previous-best seeding
highlighting a result merely because p < 0.05 or because a harder case is harder
